title: Morphisms of constructible etale module sheaves descend along affine inverse limits
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $X$ and projections $p_i:X\to X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, fix $i\in I$, and let $P_i,Q_i$ be constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $(X_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Write $t_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ for the transition morphism when $j\ge i$, and put $P_j=t_{ji}^{-1}P_i$ and $Q_j=t_{ji}^{-1}Q_i$. All inverse images are module inverse images over the constant ring sheaves, and all morphisms below are $\Lambda$-linear [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Use the canonical inverse-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] to identify $p_j^{-1}P_j$ with $p_i^{-1}P_i$, and likewise for $Q_i$.

(1) Every morphism $a:p_i^{-1}P_i\to p_i^{-1}Q_i$ is the inverse image of a morphism $a_j:P_j\to Q_j$ for some $j\ge i$, under these comparisons.

(2) If $a,b:P_i\to Q_i$ have equal inverse images on $X$, then $t_{ji}^{-1}a=t_{ji}^{-1}b$ for some $j\ge i$.

No Noetherian hypothesis on the schemes is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09YU, label lemma-category-is-colimit, part (3): the Faithful and Fully faithful paragraphs, specialized to finite commutative coefficient rings; not the essential-surjectivity assertion

proof.text: Apply the finite affine free presentation theorem to $P_i$ on the qcqs scheme $X_i$. Write $B_i\xrightarrow{d_i}A_i\xrightarrow{q_i}P_i\to0$, where $A_i=\bigoplus_{r=1}^n j_{U_r!}\underline\Lambda$ and $B_i=\bigoplus_{s=1}^m j_{V_s!}\underline\Lambda$, with all $U_r,V_s$ affine etale over $X_i$, and $q_i$ a cokernel of $d_i$. At every later stage and on $X$ use inverse image to define $A,B,d,q$. Exact additive inverse image preserves this cokernel and these finite sums. The composition comparisons identify their subsequent pullbacks with the pullbacks directly from $i$. In particular each $q$ is an epimorphism, and a map out of $A$ vanishing on $d$ factors uniquely through $q$.

source.place: Tags 09YU (lemma-category-is-colimit), proof of (3), and 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules), affine presentation

proof.text: For any transition or projection $h:T\to X_i$, the free-module base-change theorem identifies $h^{-1}j_{W!}\underline\Lambda$ with $j_{W_T!}\underline\Lambda$ and identifies maps from it to $h^{-1}Q_i$ with sections on $W_T$. This correspondence is natural in the target. More explicitly, for a later pullback $k$, a map represented by $s$ becomes the map represented by $\eta_k(s)$: this is exactly the generating-section identity in the cited free-module theorem. If the target is itself a pullback, compose with the canonical comparison $k^{-1}h^{-1}Q_i\cong(hk)^{-1}Q_i$. The resulting section map is precisely $\rho$ in the section-colimit theorem, since both are defined by this unit followed by that composition comparison. Thus maps from any pulled-back finite sum $A_i$ or $B_i$ are determined by their finitely many generating sections, and further pullback acts on these sections by $\rho$.

source.place: Tags 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) and 09YQ (theorem-colimit), degree zero; the section comparison used in 09YU Fully faithful

proof.text: We will use the following direct test for maps from either of the fixed finite free sums. Suppose $l\ge i$ and $u,v:t_{li}^{-1}A_i\to Q_l$ become equal on $X$. For each $U_r$ the corresponding sections $s_r,t_r\in Q_l(U_r\times_{X_i}X_l)$ have equal images on the limit by step 2. Apply section continuity to the original affine object $U_r$ and sheaf $Q_i$, with base index $i$. Write $\Phi_r$ for its bijective colimit-to-section map and $\iota_l$ for the stage-$l$ colimit map. Then $\Phi_r(\iota_l(s_r-t_r))=\rho_l(s_r)-\rho_l(t_r)=0$, so injectivity gives $\iota_l(s_r-t_r)=0$. The elementwise zero criterion gives $k_r\ge l$ where this difference is zero, hence where the two sections coincide. Directedness gives a single $k\ge k_r$ for all $r$; the transition identities for $\rho$ preserve those equalities at $k$. Step 2 and the finite coproduct universal property give $t_{kl}^{-1}u=t_{kl}^{-1}v$. The identical argument applies with the family $V_s$ and $B_i$. With an empty family there is only one map and take $k=l$. Notice that no constructibility of the free sums at later stages, nor of $Q_l$, was needed.

source.place: Tag 09YU, faithful argument expanded using 09YQ (theorem-colimit), degree zero; Algebra 00D6/00D7 for eventual equality

proof.text: To prove (2), precompose the given $a,b:P_i\to Q_i$ with $q_i$. Their inverse images after precomposition are equal. Apply the test of step 3 to $a q_i,b q_i:A_i\to Q_i$ to obtain a stage $j$ where $a_j q_j=b_j q_j$. Since $q_j$ remains a cokernel, it is an epimorphism: cancelling $q_j$ gives $a_j=b_j$. These are exactly $t_{ji}^{-1}a$ and $t_{ji}^{-1}b$, with the comparisons fixed above.

source.place: Tag 09YU, Faithful and proof of (3); finite presentation replaces the equality-locus argument

proof.text: For (1), start with $a:P_X\to Q_X$. By step 2 each component of $a q_X:A_X\to Q_X$ corresponds to a section $s_r\in Q_X(U_r\times_{X_i}X)$. The section-colimit theorem gives $j_r\ge i$ and a section $s_{r,j_r}\in Q_{j_r}(U_r\times_{X_i}X_{j_r})$ mapping to $s_r$. Choose one $j\ge j_r$ for all $r$ and transport these sections by $\rho_{j j_r}$. The cocone identities ensure their images are still $s_r$. The free-module evaluation bijection and the finite coproduct universal property assemble them into $b_j:A_j\to Q_j$. By step 2 its pullback is $a q_X$. If the generator family is empty, take $j=i$ and the unique map from the empty coproduct.

source.place: Tag 09YU, Fully faithful and proof of (3), lifting each generating section by 09YQ and taking a finite upper bound

proof.text: The pullback of $b_j d_j:B_j\to Q_j$ is $(a q_X)d_X=a(q_Xd_X)=0$. Apply the $B_i$ version of the test in step 3 to $b_j d_j$ and the zero map, obtaining $k\ge j$ with $b_k d_k=0$. Since $q_k$ is a cokernel of $d_k$, there is a unique $a_k:P_k\to Q_k$ with $a_k q_k=b_k$. Write $C_P:p_k^{-1}P_k\xrightarrow{\sim}P_X$ and $C_Q:p_k^{-1}Q_k\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_X$ for the fixed comparisons. Pulling back $a_kq_k=b_k$ and using their naturality gives $(C_Q\circ p_k^{-1}(a_k)\circ C_P^{-1})q_X=a q_X$. Cancel the epimorphism $q_X$ to obtain $C_Q\circ p_k^{-1}(a_k)\circ C_P^{-1}=a$, exactly the inverse-image equality required in (1). This proves (1). All constructed arrows are morphisms in the module-sheaf category, so they are $\Lambda$-linear throughout.
